claim: In the matching retail DLL, FormAnimator.StartOpponentAnmM (MethodDef 0x06004E77) takes three Int32 parameters named en, anm_idx, and mp. It resolves arg1 through PlayerMan.GetPlObj and returns early if that selected Player is absent; separately resolves arg3 through PlayerMan.GetPlObj; invokes ReqBasicAnm(this.BasicSkillID, false, -1) on the arg1-selected Player animator; writes the host/current-skill/type/index/terrain/end fields on that selected Player/animator; applies the exact numeric terrain filter; conditionally copies arg3-selected Player X/Y position and direction when that second lookup is present; and calls DropWeapon on the arg1-selected Player. In verified R6 raw capture bytes, all 68 observed StartOpponentAnmM PRE calls pair with POST calls and are directly nested under InitAnimation. In all 68, raw arg2 is 2, raw arg3 equals the parent InitAnimation target, raw arg1 equals both the nested ReqBasicAnm owner_slot and direct DropWeapon owner_slot, and the DropWeapon snapshot records AnmHostPlayer equal to the StartOpponentAnmM host owner_slot. The three recorded slot integers host owner, arg1, and arg3 are pairwise distinct in all 68 observations.
